channel.description: Recent content on Nithin Kamath's personal homepage

item.title: When do traders use Kill Switch the most?
item.description: We were looking at when traders use Kill Switch the most. Kill Switch is a feature we offer to disable a specific trading segment or take a break from trading. I would’ve guessed that Kill Switch requests would go up when markets fall, but that doesn’t seem to be the case. Direction barely matters, what matters is volatility. Across millions of Kill Switch requests this year, our busiest week was during an 8.

item.title: Blobasaur an open-source storage engine built at Zerodha
item.description: Our tech team has built and open-sourced a distributed, high-performance “blob” storage engine. We needed to store UI and workspace preferences for millions of users, especially after the launch of Kite Terminal mode. Unlike small structured data, the data are “blobs”, anywhere from a few KBs to a few MBs. We looked around for a database that was simple to run and built specifically for this but couldn’t find one. So we built our own.

item.title: LIQUIDCASE is now India’s largest liquid ETF
item.description: It’s been nearly 3 years since we launched LIQUIDCASE, and it is now the largest liquid ETF in India, with nearly ₹12,000 crore in AUM. We built it to fix one problem. Other liquid ETFs paid out returns as tiny dividends every day, either in cash or as additional units, and both were a pain to deal with. First, you had to keep track of all the dividends to calculate your returns, and then filing taxes on top of this was a nightmare.

item.title: If nature has no price, does it have no value?
item.description: I recently watched the brilliant documentary How to Live on Earth, and I think all of us should watch it. It left me with a lot of questions, but one stuck with me: what is the value of a tree? A lot of people would say its value is in what it becomes once it’s cut down: timber, firewood, paper. Think about the absurdity of that. The tree is worth more dead than alive.

item.title: Greenjoules - Turning agricultural waste into fuel
item.description: It’s that time of the year again when air quality becomes a topic of national discussion because of Delhi. One of the big contributors during this season is stubble burning in Punjab and the surrounding regions. On the worst days, it can account for over a third of Delhi’s pollution. Delhi gets most of the attention, partly because it has one of the densest networks of air quality sensors. But many cities across North India are just as bad.

item.title: Portfolio Performance Curve on Console
item.description: Looking at the absolute returns of your portfolio doesn’t tell you much. You need to compare it to a reasonable benchmark to know how well you have done. You can do this with the portfolio performance curve on Console. If you’ve beaten your benchmark, then good. If not, you’re probably better off investing in some index funds. The only issue is you can’t flaunt your index fund investments 😬

item.title: The post-COVID transformation of US markets
item.description: The rate at which the US markets have changed (mutated) since COVID is nuts. Before COVID, the last major “innovation”, if you want to call it that, was 0-day options. But since then, you’ve had crypto trading, and with that, stablecoins, derivatives, NFTs, and DeFi, not to forget shitcoins. For all the jokes and memes, crypto is fully mainstream now, with almost full regulatory blessing, with futures, ETFs, etc. Then you have prediction markets.

item.title: Why zero brokerage for Muhurat trading session?
item.description: Someone on the team asked me the story behind why brokerage is free for all trades during the Diwali Muhurat trading session. Honestly, there isn’t a backstory. We kept brokerage free as a way of saying thank you to all the customers for trading with someone like us, who was very new at the time. And in the 16 years since, we’ve kept it the same for every Muhurat session.🪔

item.title: Opening an NRI account is getting easier
item.description: In August, I’d written about SEBI’s proposal to simplify account opening for NRIs. Good to see that the changes have now been finalised. For years, one of the biggest hurdles for NRIs wanting to invest in India has been account opening. While those with existing KYC could open accounts digitally, anyone abroad needing fresh KYC had to get documents attested by a notary or the Indian embassy, courier physical copies to India, and wait weeks for the account to open.

item.title: Instant withdrawals update
item.description: We’ve increased our instant withdrawal limit from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh. It’s now available from 9 AM to 6 PM, including weekends and market holidays. Since 2024, we’ve processed nearly ₹1 lakh crore in instant payouts, completely free🙂

item.title: Commodity traders rise as equity F&O participation falls
item.description: The increase in the number of traders on MCX (commodities) is interesting. While the number of equity F&O traders has declined from 1.06 crore in FY25 to 85 lakh in FY26, the number of commodity traders has increased from 13 lakh to almost 21 lakh. I think this coincides with the growth of options trading on MCX. I also wonder how much of this is because of the heightened volatility in commodities like crude, natural gas, gold, and silver, and brokers pushing commodity options more after equity markets close.

item.title: The Back Office with Vinay
item.description: In 2012, before we had a tech team, our second tech vendor was KuVi, a services company Vinay Kumar C started right after college. Vinay was introduced to us by Renuka, who’s now an AVP on our support team. She said she had a friend who could take care of all our tech needs, from hosting our website to building our first CRM and pretty much everything else. We said yes, partly because they were charging us just ₹15,000 a month.

item.title: Jio Platforms and a record day for delivery selling
item.description: Yesterday was probably a record day for equity delivery selling, thanks to Jio Platforms, with investors selling shares after the listing. By the way, our customers would have saved anywhere between ₹1.5 crore and ₹10 crore in brokerage alone, based on what others charge. This doesn’t include potential additional savings on DP charges, ours is one of the lowest. Our brokerage on equity delivery is still zero.🙂

item.title: Unintended consequences of higher STT and F&O curbs
item.description: Across Zerodha, here’s roughly the percentage of individual traders who are profitable: Futures: ≈50% Option sellers: ≈40% Option buyers: ≈10% MTF: too early to tell, considering it’s a new product One of the unintended consequences of increasing STT and all the other measures to curb F&O speculation is that they may have pushed traders toward even riskier trading behaviour. Yes, in theory, losses from buying options are limited to the premium paid.

item.title: What are you using Kite APIs for?
item.description: Now that Kite APIs are free, how are you using them with AI agents? What have you built? AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex have made it much easier for traders and investors to build their own tools, even without much coding experience. We’re also seeing more people use Kite APIs because of these coding agents.

item.title: Intermission by The Ken - the story of TCS
item.description: History doesn’t repeat itself, but it often rhymes. With everything happening around AI, it feels like we’ve seen versions of this story before. Technologies change, industries get disrupted, and businesses that once seemed permanent disappear. The latest episode of Intermission by The Ken is on TCS, and one thing stood out to me. In the 1960s, India had only a few dozen computers, and even that was enough for unions to protest, fearing they would take away jobs.

item.title: History may not repeat itself, but it often rhymes
item.description: In a world where growth and revenues are almost always prioritised over risk, I think it helps to look back at history and remind ourselves of the follies of humankind. After all, history may not repeat itself, but it often rhymes. I just finished reading 1873 by Liaquat Ahamed, about the Vienna stock market crash that eventually triggered a global financial crisis. I had read 1929 by Andrew Ross Sorkin last year, which explores a similar theme.

item.title: Rainmatter Originals - Turning wastewater into a resource
item.description: Recently, I wrote about how serious our water problem is getting. This year’s weak monsoon has made it worse, and in Bengaluru, for example, that means dry borewells and expensive tankers. But we’re also wasting water we’ve already cleaned. Large apartments have to treat their own sewage, but only 20–30% of that water gets used. The rest goes down the drain. Meanwhile, IT parks and factories a few kilometers away are buying tanker water for their cooling towers.

item.title: Why NPS works well for long-term retirement investing
item.description: When you’re in your 20s or 30s, retirement is probably the last thing on your mind. But that’s also when you have the biggest advantage when it comes to investing: time. The challenge, however, isn’t just starting early. It’s staying invested for decades without dipping into your retirement savings along the way. One of the most underrated aspects of retirement investing is having money that’s not easily accessible. This forced discipline can make a huge difference over the long term.

item.title: The other side of MTF growth
item.description: Most of the growth in the industry’s MTF book is in small and microcaps. These are the stocks where liquidity tends to dry up first when markets either fall or go sideways, like they are right now😬
